semantic_invariants.statement: Semantic transactions address stable SplashMX IDs/loci, never transport/Godot/runtime handles.
Replica convergence is necessary but every materialized document must also validate semantically.
Independent concurrent loci merge regardless of relay arrival order or duplicate delivery.
Incompatible same-locus intent remains an explicit conflict with the prior coherent value active.
Thing delete/edit is tombstone remove-wins and stale work cannot resurrect the identity.
Concurrent incompatible reparent operations hold the prior legal structure.
Definition/instance conflicts are scoped by actual DefinitionId and element identity.
Stable-port connection edits commute with unrelated structural movement.
Port removal versus a concurrent connection through that port is an atomic explicit conflict.
Thing deletion remove-wins over concurrent connection creation that names the deleted endpoint.
Connection endpoints and ports are validated before a transaction can materialize.
Independent timeline keyframes merge while the same semantic key/time locus conflicts.
Overlapping multi-Thing grouping commands are atomic and never half-materialize.
Compatible component updates preserve concurrent valid local overlays.
Component updates that invalidate concurrent local work are held rather than consuming it.
Connection deletion prevents same-ConnectionId resurrection; conflicting same-ID creates are explicit.
Offline valid edits survive reunion and converge without a cloud copy silently winning.
Transaction replay is idempotent; same-ID/different-content is corruption and rejected.
Missing causal ancestors pend dependent work rather than guessing an order or dropping it.
Selective undo/redo are new causal edits with current preconditions and preserve unrelated remote work.
Permission policy is revalidated after offline work; stale-authority edits remain recoverable history but not shared state.
Presence, cursors and selections are transient and absent from durable history/canonical state.
Schema-incompatible history is quarantined until deterministic migration exists.
Known-unloaded, tombstoned and unknown targets remain distinct; known-unloaded work may pend.
Conflict resolution is a later causal semantic transaction and does not rewrite proposal history.
Runtime-multiplayer fields/capability/session handles are recursively rejected from collaboration data.
A stable AssetId selects one indivisible digest/source/audio/provenance/licence/derivation revision; concurrent replacements never field-mix.
Whole-transaction validation dominates partial operation success; invalid composite edits roll back atomically.

observed_repairs.statement: Definition/instance conflict detection must include actual DefinitionId, not only a coincident element name.
Concurrent Thing deletion and connection creation naming that Thing is a tombstone remove-wins conflict; the new connection is held.
Every transaction candidate is semantically document-validated before commit, including stable connection endpoints/ports; failure holds the whole transaction.
Tombstoning a Thing tombstones its incident live connections in the same atomic semantic transaction so canonical state has no dangling active edge.

protected_semantics.rule: one complete revision alternative; no field-wise merge across competing replacements

residuals: browser/native persistent store and crash recovery
multi-version operation migration at production scale
